small_guidance:
- The softmax tail kernel processes S=64×128×128=1,048,576 elements per (B,C) row in one program; split each row across multiple programs with a two-pass reduction (atomic or auxiliary buffer) or at least raise BLOCK to 4096/8192 and num_warps=16 to better saturate memory bandwidth. Also fuse the clamp with the conv_transpose bias-add epilogue if possible.
- Try `num_warps=16, num_stages=3, BLOCK=4096` autotune configs on the clamp+softmax kernel; the row is huge so wider tiles reduce loop overhead.
- Avoid recomputing clamp twice (pass 1 and pass 2); cache values via a single-pass online softmax that stores partial exponentials only once, or write clamped values to a scratch buffer in pass 1 and just read+exp in pass 2.
large_guidance:
- The dominant cost is the ConvTranspose3d (out shape 32×64×64×128×128 ≈ 1G elements), not the softmax tail. A from-scratch rewrite should replace `self.conv_transpose` with a custom Triton scatter-add (or gather) kernel that fuses avg_pool input gather, conv_transpose, clamp into one kernel writing the pre-softmax tensor.
- Strategy: one program per (B, OC tile, output-spatial tile); for each output voxel gather the valid (id_div, ih_div, iw_div, kd, kh, kw) tuples via the divisibility test, and compute the pooled input on-the-fly (mean of 8 raw voxels) — fuse avg_pool + convT + clamp into a single GEMM-style kernel using BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SP=32, with IC as the reduction axis (use tl.dot on [BLOCK_SP, IC]·[IC, BLOCK_OC] tiles after gathering pooled input into a register tile).
- Then keep the softmax+scale as a separate fused kernel but parallelize the per-row reduction across multiple SMs (split-K style) since each row has ~1M elements — a single program per row leaves the GPU underutilized.
